body.p: When the DITAhistoryDITA standard was first published by OASIS in 2005, the publishing landscape looked very different from today. Print was still the dominant delivery channel for technical documentation, and the idea of a single source producing multiple output formats was more aspiration than reality for most organizations.

Two decades later, the world has changed profoundly. Readers expect content on their phones, tablets, and e-readers. Accessibility is no longer an afterthought but a legal requirement in many jurisdictions. And the EPUBadoptionEPUB format — once a niche concern of trade publishers — has become the universal container for reflowable digital content, supported by every major reading platform from Apple Books to Kobo to Thorium Reader.

What has not changed is the fundamental challenge: how do you take structured, semantically rich content and transform it into a publication that is both technically correct and aesthetically pleasing? This is the question that the dita2epub plugindita2epub plugin answers.

I first encountered this project when searching for a modern EPUB 3 transformation for DITA-OT. The existing options were either outdated, incomplete, or produced output that failed EPUBCheck validation. The dita2epub plugin took a different approach: start from the EPUB 3.3 specification and work backward, ensuring that every output file is valid, accessible, and well-structured from the ground up.

What impressed me most was the attention to detail. Footnotes with proper backlinks. Localized labels for notes and navigation in eleven languages. Font obfuscation using the IDPF algorithm. Automatic generation of indexes, glossaries, and lists of figures — all from standard DITA markup, with no custom extensions required.

This handbook is both documentation and demonstration. Every page you read was generated by the very plugin it describes. The cover page, the table of contents, the index at the back — all produced automatically from the DITA source. If you are holding a well-formatted, accessible EPUB right now, then the plugin has done its job.

I encourage you to read this book not just as a manual, but as a proof of concept. Explore the source files. Modify the parameters. Break things and fix them. That is how good tools become great tools.
— Jane Smith, Technical Publishing Consultant, March 2026
